name: Private credit stress
value: Fund redemption caps persist; no forced sales
summary: Large private credit funds keep limiting redemptions; no forced asset sales or bank losses found as of 12 Nov
state: Large semi-liquid private credit funds have repeatedly limited withdrawals this year; KKR's private credit fund went above its 5% cap to meet requests in early October (Bloomberg, 5 Oct), and the rating agency KBRA said gates were working as designed (16 Sep). Searches on 12 Nov found no new wave of simultaneous gates, forced asset sales or losses spreading to banks or insurers, so Watch holds.
for_you: Investors in semi-liquid private credit and BDC funds are exposed to withdrawal limits. Pension and insurance holders have indirect exposure. Banks and insurers have not reported material losses from the sector.
rubric_hit: Watch: large funds limit redemptions; no several-fund gating at once, forced sales or bank/insurer losses (Alert line)

sources.title: Bloomberg — KKR private credit fund exceeds 5% redemption cap to fulfil withdrawals
KBRA — Private credit: why gates are good for investors

why: Private credit has grown fast outside bank regulation; its losses surface late and can spill into banks, insurers and pension funds.
drivers: Defaults among leveraged mid-sized borrowers, payment-in-kind interest, fund redemption requests, bank lending to funds.

rubric.alert: Several large funds gate at once, forced asset sales, or losses spreading to banks or insurers.
rubric.watch: A large fund limits redemptions, listed BDCs trade at wide discounts to NAV, or a cluster of borrower defaults with heavy losses.
rubric.normal: No notable fund gates, defaults or markdowns beyond the routine.
